location: src/haute/_execute_lazy.py:1903-1904 (multi-port emit branch of _execute_eager_core), consumed at src/haute/executor.py:1131-1137 (_column_infos_for_node)
title: Multi-port apiInput source node reports zero columns in its own preview (empty output_columns shadows the first-port fallback)
description: In the multi-port emit branch of `_execute_eager_core`, a source that returns `dict[port_label, DataFrame]` has `output_columns[nid] = []` and `available_columns[nid] = []` hard-set (lines 1903-1904). That empty list flows out as `EagerResult.output_columns` and becomes `output_cols` in `executor._eager_execute`. When the preview builder renders the source node itself, `_column_infos_for_node` (executor.py:1131) does `full_output = output_cols.get(node_id)`, gets `[]`, and because `[] is not None` is True it sets `columns = []` and never reaches the `elif df is not None` branch (line 1134) that would derive columns from the representative first-port DataFrame. The result: the multi-port apiInput node's NodeResult has `column_count == 0` and `columns == []` even though `df = next(iter(df.values()))` (executor.py:1182-1185) is a real DataFrame with columns and `row_count` is reported correctly. This directly defeats the documented intent at executor.py:1179-1181 ('use the first port's frame as a representative'). Single-port apiInput is unaffected because it returns a bare DataFrame and takes the normal path that populates `output_columns` (line 1933).
evidence: _execute_eager_core multi-port branch: `output_columns[nid] = []` (line 1904) then `continue` (line 1907), so the normal `output_columns[nid] = full_output_columns` (line 1933) is skipped. executor._column_infos_for_node: `full_output = output_cols.get(node_id)` -> `[]`; `if full_output is not None:` is taken for an empty list, so `columns = [ColumnInfo(n,d) for n,d in []] == []`; the `elif df is not None` first-port fallback is dead for this node. Existing test test_apiinput_multi_port_runtime.py::test_two_consumers_different_ports_dont_collide_on_column_cache only asserts columns on the POLARS *consumer* nodes (c_policies/c_drivers, lines 411-420), and the single-port test (lines 184-189) asserts only status/row_count on `api` — no test asserts `results['api'].columns`/`column_count` for a multi-port source, so the gap is uncovered.
